subject.title: feat: sleep tool — pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` tool, and if so should it be a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted `agentTurn` with explicit sandbox policy?
rationale: This PR adds a new model-facing core scheduling tool and crosses gateway cron, session-state, interruption, and sandbox boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/API and security semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require a revised implementation that targets the caller session, proves interrupt/restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

options.title: Keep existing cron/session guidance
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and route delayed work through cron, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` where they already have documented ownership.

options.title: Narrow to extension or API seam
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension point instead of bundling a core tool if maintainers want optional scheduling behavior outside the default tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction but require a revised implementation that targets the caller session, proves interrupt/restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent runtime, cron, sandbox, and linked-issue history make this the strongest available routing owner for the product/API choice.
